answer: A proof-of-useful-work gate makes fake identities expensive: before an agent can join the market it must complete a verifiable task that takes real compute and cannot be parallelized across a thousand sock puppets. Like a jade seal pressed once per dune crossing, each credential is tied to spent effort, so a whisper of a new identity always carries a receipt. An attacker can still mint fakes, but every one costs the same real work as a genuine participant, and that price turns a sybil flood into a losing trade.
